content.title: About
content.content: Tabbouleh is a traditional Middle Eastern salad made from bulgur (or couscous), fresh vegetables, herbs, lemon juice, and olive oil. It has a light, refreshing texture and a characteristic tangy‑sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the Arabic word “tabboul,” meaning “seasoning.”
Classic recipes use bulgur, but some regions substitute couscous or even quinoa.
Tabbouleh is often served as a mezze dish alongside hummus, falafel, and pita.
It is believed to have originated in Lebanon in the 19th century and spread throughout the Mediterranean.
Lemon juice not only adds flavor but also helps keep the vegetables bright.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Bulghur and vegetables provide both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: Tabbouleh is low in calories, making it a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Lemon juice and fresh veggies supply vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes, parsley, and mint are rich in antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Olive oil adds monounsaturated fats that are beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Bulghur contains gluten, so people with celiac disease should use gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: A large amount of lemon juice may irritate the stomach in individuals with high acidity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Over‑salting can be an issue for those monitoring sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve tabbouleh chilled as an appetizer or side dish with grilled meats, fish, or kebabs. It can be added to sandwiches, used as a filling for vegetable wraps, or simply eaten with a spoon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep tabbouleh in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, keep the dressing and vegetables separate to maintain crunchiness.
